slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you calmly
self-assured in any room
Arriving without rushing. Leave a few minutes early so you walk in calm, not out of breath. A relaxed entrance sets how people see you for the rest of the evening.
Greeting people with a pause. Look at them, smile, then say hello. That one second of stillness makes you look sure of yourself before you've said anything.
Holding your drink low and still. At your side, not in front of your chest like a shield. Calm hands send a quiet message that you feel at home in the room.
Speaking to the whole group, not just one person. Let your eyes move around the circle while you talk. It shows ease and makes everyone feel included.
Before: worrying what to talk about in a new room. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calm feeling that I always have something to say.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: worrying what to talk about in a new room. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Now I feel calm, I always have something to say.

slides.texte_overlay: Letting others have the spotlight. You don't need to win every conversation. Asking someone else to tell their story shows more confidence than telling yours.
Being comfortable not knowing people. Standing alone for a minute is fine. Look around, enjoy the room, and let conversations come to you naturally.
